Backend: 23/23 new tests + 13/13 regression tests all pass. Found + fixed a P0 crash on /commissions/{id} caused by useEffect returning a Promise. After fix, CommissionTimeline renders with all 7 stages and correct color coding (green=done, orange=pending, red=declined).

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED. `useEffect(load, [id])` where load returned a Promise caused React to try calling the Promise as cleanup → 'destroy is not a function' + 'Cannot destructure basename ... useContext(...) as it is null' at LinkWithRef. This crashed the entire /commissions/{id} route including the new CommissionTimeline. Fixed by wrapping in arrow function: `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [id])`.

rca_of_the_issue: P0 CRASH on /commissions/{id}: React error overlay with 'destroy is not a function' + 'Cannot destructure basename of useContext(...) as it is null at LinkWithRef'. RCA: Commissions.js line 168 was `useEffect(load, [id])` where load = `() => api.get(...).then((r) => setC(r.data)).catch(...)`. That returns a Promise. React 18 interprets the return value of a useEffect callback as the cleanup function — since a Promise is not a function, on unmount/re-run React attempts `promise()` which throws 'destroy is not a function'. The unhandled error then destabilizes the React tree, causing the next render's <Link> to see useContext(RouterContext) === null and throw the basename destructure error. Reproduction: navigate to any /commissions/{id}. Mitigation: wrap in an anonymous arrow — `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [id])`. Applied and verified — page now renders cleanly with 0 console errors and all 7 timeline stages visible with correct color coding.
